_about: Plain-language notes for common blood tests. Every line is taken from the source page named in its entry, fetched 24 November 2026. No reference ranges are stored here on purpose: those are read from each patient's own report, because they differ by lab and method. Nothing here is a diagnosis.

haemoglobin.what: Haemoglobin is the iron-rich protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen; this test measures how much of it is in your blood.
haemoglobin.high: A higher result can be a sign of lung or heart disease or of polycythaemia, and is often seen with dehydration, smoking or living at high altitude.
haemoglobin.low: A lower result can be a sign of anaemia, low iron or vitamin B-12, thalassaemia, blood loss or liver disease.
haemoglobin.ask: What could be causing my haemoglobin result, and do I need follow-up tests such as iron or vitamin B-12 levels?

packed_cell_volume.what: This test shows what share of your blood is made up of red blood cells, the cells that carry oxygen around your body.
packed_cell_volume.high: A higher result is often seen with dehydration, and can be a sign of the body making too many red blood cells, as in some lung or heart conditions.
packed_cell_volume.low: A lower result can be a sign of anaemia or blood loss, and is also commonly seen in pregnancy because of the extra fluid in the body.
packed_cell_volume.ask: What level is normal for me given my age, sex, smoking and altitude, and do I need a full blood count or iron tests?

mcv.what: Mean corpuscular volume, or MCV, is the average size of your red blood cells.
mcv.high: A higher MCV, meaning larger cells, can be a sign of anaemia from a vitamin B deficiency, or of liver disease.
mcv.low: A lower MCV, meaning smaller cells, can be a sign of iron deficiency anaemia or of thalassaemia, an inherited blood disorder.
mcv.ask: What do my MCV and other red cell results mean together, and do I need tests for iron or vitamin levels?

rdw.what: Red cell distribution width, or RDW, measures how much your red blood cells differ from one another in size and volume.
rdw.high: A result outside the range means there are differences in the size of your red blood cells; on its own this is not enough for a diagnosis.
rdw.low: A result outside the range means there are differences in the size of your red blood cells; on its own this is not enough for a diagnosis.
rdw.ask: What do my RDW and MCV results mean when read together with the rest of my blood count?

total_leucocyte_count.what: This test counts the white blood cells in your blood; these cells are part of your immune system and help fight infection.
total_leucocyte_count.high: A higher count is often seen with infection, inflammation, allergy or tissue damage, and can also follow smoking, stress, pregnancy or a reaction to a medicine.
total_leucocyte_count.low: A lower count can be a sign of bone marrow affected by infection, disease or treatments such as chemotherapy, or of some autoimmune conditions.
total_leucocyte_count.ask: What might explain my white cell count, and do I need a differential count or other follow-up tests?

platelet_count.what: Platelets are tiny blood cells, made in bone marrow, that help your blood clot; this test counts how many you have.
platelet_count.high: A higher count can make blood clot more than needed, and is often seen with infection, inflammation, anaemia, heavy blood loss or some cancers.
platelet_count.low: A lower count can lead to easy bruising or bleeding, and can be seen with viral infection, autoimmune disease, vitamin B12 deficiency, cirrhosis or bone marrow problems.
platelet_count.ask: Do my platelet results explain my bruising or bleeding, and do any of my medicines affect platelets?

tsh.what: TSH is the hormone your pituitary gland uses to tell your thyroid how much thyroid hormone to make; this test measures it.
tsh.high: A higher TSH often suggests an underactive thyroid, meaning the thyroid is not making enough hormone; rarely it reflects a pituitary problem.
tsh.low: A lower TSH often suggests an overactive thyroid, and can also dip for a time in early pregnancy or during a serious unrelated illness.
tsh.ask: Do my TSH results point to a thyroid problem, and which other thyroid tests do you recommend?

free_t3.what: Free T3 measures the active, unbound form of triiodothyronine, a thyroid hormone, which can enter the body tissues that need it.
free_t3.high: A higher result can be a sign of an overactive thyroid, meaning the thyroid is making too much hormone.
free_t3.low: A lower result can be a sign of an underactive thyroid, though this test is not commonly used to check for that.
free_t3.ask: What do my T3, free T4 and TSH results mean together, and do I need any follow-up testing?

free_t4.what: Free T4 measures the active, unbound form of thyroxine, the main hormone the thyroid makes, that enters your body tissues.
free_t4.high: A higher result can be a sign of an overactive thyroid, and is also seen with some stages of thyroiditis, too much iodine, or too much thyroid medicine.
free_t4.low: A lower result can be a sign of an underactive thyroid, and is also seen after treatment for an overactive thyroid or thyroid cancer.
free_t4.ask: What do my free T4 and TSH results mean together, and could any of my medicines or supplements be affecting them?

fasting_blood_sugar.what: This test measures glucose, the main sugar your body uses for energy, in blood taken after at least eight hours without food.
fasting_blood_sugar.high: A higher result can be a sign of prediabetes or diabetes, and is sometimes seen with thyroid, pancreas or adrenal problems, serious illness, or certain medicines.
fasting_blood_sugar.low: A lower result is often linked to diabetes medicines, eating too little or extra activity, and less often to liver, kidney, adrenal, pituitary or thyroid problems.
fasting_blood_sugar.ask: What does my fasting blood sugar mean for me, and do I need another test to confirm it?

hba1c.what: HbA1c shows your average blood sugar over the past few months, because glucose sticks to haemoglobin inside your red blood cells.
hba1c.high: A higher result can be a sign of prediabetes or diabetes, and is usually confirmed with another test such as fasting glucose.
hba1c.low: The source does not describe what a lower result means; ask your doctor.
hba1c.ask: What HbA1c is healthy for me, and do I need a second test to confirm this result?

total_cholesterol.what: Total cholesterol is the overall amount of cholesterol, a waxy fat-like substance, in your blood, counting both the LDL and HDL kinds.
total_cholesterol.high: A higher result usually means steps to bring cholesterol down are advised, as it adds to the risk of heart and artery disease.
total_cholesterol.low: A low total cholesterol is not described as a concern; low LDL and high HDL are generally good for heart health.
total_cholesterol.ask: Which of my lipid results are outside the healthy range for me, and how often should I be retested?

ldl_cholesterol.what: LDL is the 'bad' cholesterol, the chief contributor to the fatty build-up that can narrow or block your arteries.
ldl_cholesterol.high: A higher LDL raises the risk of coronary artery and other heart disease, which can lead to heart attack, stroke or blocked blood flow to the limbs.
ldl_cholesterol.low: A low LDL is generally good for heart health.
ldl_cholesterol.ask: Was my LDL measured directly or calculated, and what does my level mean for my heart risk?

hdl_cholesterol.what: HDL is the 'good' cholesterol; it helps clear LDL cholesterol out of your blood.
hdl_cholesterol.high: A higher HDL is generally good for heart health and may help lower the risk of heart attack or stroke.
hdl_cholesterol.low: A lower HDL is flagged as a concern, because it gives less of that protection against heart attack and stroke.
hdl_cholesterol.ask: Is my HDL low for my age and sex, and what changes would help raise it?

triglycerides.what: Triglycerides are a type of fat your body uses for energy; this test measures how much of them is in your blood.
triglycerides.high: A higher result can add to the risk of heart disease, stroke and metabolic syndrome, and very high levels raise the risk of sudden pancreatitis.
triglycerides.low: Triglyceride levels that are too low are very uncommon, and the source says nothing further about them.
triglycerides.ask: Do I need to fast before this test, and what do my triglycerides mean for my heart risk?

serum_creatinine.what: Creatinine is a normal waste product made by your muscles; this blood test is used to judge how well your kidneys filter waste.
serum_creatinine.high: A higher result can be a sign of kidney disease or injury, but is also seen with dehydration, hard exercise, muscle injury or a diet high in meat.
serum_creatinine.low: A lower result is uncommon, and can be seen with poor nutrition, loss of muscle, or serious liver disease.
serum_creatinine.ask: What do my creatinine and eGFR results say about my kidney health, and do I need repeat or additional kidney tests?
